records.text: Felder Stover is a weaponsmith who offers goods to browse through both the standard merchant and repair interactions.
Borgus Stoutarm is a gryphon master who handles flight inquiries. When attacked, he calls for guards and summons an enraged gryphon, giving his routine travel role a sharp defensive exception.
Gabrielle Chase is a food and drink merchant with browseable goods and a questgiver interaction.
Gruna is a food and drink merchant with browseable goods and a questgiver interaction.
A Blackrock Soldier is a Blackrock combatant whose recorded combat responses include Revenge and Improved Blocking.
A Blackrock Sorcerer is a Blackrock spellcaster who hurls fireballs.
A Blackrock slayer, this humanoid fights with a heavy weapon and uses Hamstring to hinder opponents.
A Blackrock warlock, this humanoid attacks with shadow magic, including Shadow Bolt, Curse of Tongues, and Immolate.
A Blackrock battlemaster, this humanoid is encountered as a combatant and uses an ability when it draws an enemy's attention.
An obsidian elemental found in the Burning Steppes region, this creature is identified by its elemental nature and obsidian form.
A greater obsidian elemental found in the Burning Steppes region, this creature is identified by its elemental nature and obsidian form.
A Firegut ogre with a blunt, aggressive combat voice, it threatens to smash or crush its opponent. It fights with a torch and shares these short battle cries with Firegut Ogre Mages.
A Firegut ogre mage with a blunt, aggressive combat voice, it threatens to smash or crush its opponent. It fights with a torch and shares these short battle cries with Firegut Ogres.

A Firegut ogre brute, this fighter voices blunt threats—“Me smash! You die!” and “I’ll crush you!” Oralius describes the Firegut ogres as allies of the Blackrock orcs, guarding Dreadmaul Rock and keeping supply lines open; this brute is one of the forces targeted in his call to cripple them.
The Thaurissan Spy is identified by its name as a Thaurissan operative. It strikes with poison and backstabs.
The Thaurissan Firewalker is identified by its name with Thaurissan. Its combat abilities are Flame Buffet and Flame Spray.
The Thaurissan Agent serves Thaurissan and shoots from range.
An elemental that attacks with Thrash.
The Black Dragonspawn is one of the dragonkin identified by Oralius as being below the ridge in the Burning Steppes, where he asks for help pushing them back. It uses Rend.
A Black Wyrmkin is a dragonkin of the Burning Steppes that attacks with fire magic, hurling fireballs.
A Flamescale Dragonspawn is a dragonkin of the Burning Steppes that blasts its foes with fire.
A Flamescale Wyrmkin is a dragonkin of the Burning Steppes that buffets its foes with flame.
A Black Drake is a dragonkin encountered in the Burning Steppes. In combat, it breathes flame at its foes.
A Scalding Drake is a dragonkin encountered in the Burning Steppes. In combat, it attacks with Flame Breath.
A Searscale Drake is a dragonkin encountered in the Burning Steppes. In combat, it attacks with Flame Breath.
A Black Broodling is a young dragonkin of the Burning Steppes that hurls fireballs.
A broodling among Blackrock Mountain’s creatures, the Scalding Broodling attacks with fireballs.
A broodling among Blackrock Mountain’s creatures, the Flamescale Broodling attacks with fireballs.

A tormented presence in the ruins of Thaurissan, this voice warns intruders away and shares fractured memories: a ritual by eight Dark Iron dwarves, a lone survivor among seven corpses, and a fiery being tied to the city's destruction. Its warnings also speak of an evil presence within the mountain.
Hematos is a dragonkin whose combat behavior includes breathing flame.
Krom'Grul is a brute who led the capture and slaughter of Sha'ni's platoon, then chained and tortured her and took her wedding nose-ring. He roars that he will smash his foes.
Thauris Balgarr is a humanoid whose combat abilities include a net and Dark Iron land mines.
Gruklash can enter a frenzy during battle.
A malfunctioning mechanical reaver that lands heavy uppercuts.
Gor'tesh is a brute lord who rules from a Blackrock orc structure west of Dreadmaul Rock and is marked for death in the campaign against the Firegut ogres. He smashes the ground and knocks foes away.

Oralius directs a staged campaign against the Firegut ogres, whom he describes as allies of the Blackrock orcs and protectors of Dreadmaul Rock's supply lines. He calls for successive attacks, culminating in displaying Gor'tesh's head on a pike atop the mountain to frighten the ogres. His mission text veers into disconnected threats and bizarre gestures; in another report he talks into a severed ogre ear.

Cyrus Therepentous is a fire-loving dragonkin who craves the heat of Blackrock’s molten depths. He demands proof of worth from those seeking the Black Dragonflight and speaks with cutting contempt, calling visitors fools or useless. His desire to taste the mountain’s flame becomes explicit in his demand for a piece of Bael’Gar’s inner fire; when presented with the essence, he eagerly snatches it and sends the bearer away.

Grark Lorkrub is a Blackrock-aligned informant whom Lexlort accuses of betraying the Thorium Brotherhood by giving Blackrock orcs vital details about its operations. During his capture and forced escort, Grark defends Blackrock’s cause, warns that its armies plan to destroy the world, and threatens those who oppose him. He resents being shackled and led, insisting he knows the way and predicting that his captors will pay for the incursion.

Maxwort Uberglint is a treasure seeker drawn to the legends of the Seven, whose knowledge he hopes will bring wealth. He has spent years pursuing the Heart of the Mountain and, unable to buy it from the Dark Iron dwarves, asks others to seize it from their vault. He values the gem immensely and wants the Seven’s tablet writings so he can uncover their secrets.

Yuka Screwspigot is pursuing her brother Ribbly, whose schemes have drained the family’s money. She sees his bounty as a way to make him worth something to the Screwspigots and asks for him to be brought back; if he resists, she accepts his head instead. Her words mix family grievance with dark amusement at the prospect of turning him in to Baron Revilgaz.

Marshal Maxwell directs Alliance intelligence and decisive strikes against Blackrock Spire. He frames the campaign as a two-front fight: Stormwind works from within while forces in the Burning Steppes attack the orcs’ doorstep. His orders target Blackrock’s command structure, and he presents the assault as retaliation for attacks on Alliance homes and families. Afterward, he anticipates a campaign against the dragon lords.

Jalinda Sprig is trying to get an expedition into Blackrock Depths, but Overmaster Pyron has badly hurt the mages she sent to investigate. She describes him as guarding the quarry entrance and asks for his removal so her crew can proceed. Learning of Lord Incendius unsettles her: she swallows hard at the thought that he serves Ragnaros, worries aloud, and says Incendius keeps raising Pyron from the ashes. She sounds anxious about the danger and short of people to send.

Helendis Riverhorn bases his response to the Blackrock worg threat on reports from his scouts: the worgs are bred, trained, and sent out from Blackrock Spire. He orders an investigation into their source and its destruction, naming Halycon as the source in his parting instruction. His appeal to Cenarius gives the mission a reverent note, and after the task he calls the corrupted beast’s suffering something not to dwell upon.

Ragged John is an unconventional, tipsy-seeming poison enthusiast who wants a live sample of Mother Smolderweb’s venom, obtained by having the adventurer poisoned. He eagerly plans to milk the sample, then jokes that it will make ale. His rough, slurred greeting fits his irreverent manner.

Mayara Brightwing is a scout working for Count Remington Ridgewell, whose family museum seeks valuable relics and art. She directs the recovery of Doomrigger’s jeweled clasp from Blackrock Spire, then asks for its delivery to Ridgewell. She also offers help retrieving another object of art for the collection.
Hahk'Zor is a humanoid of the Burning Steppes.
Gorgon'och is a hostile brute who roars that he will smash and crush his foes; in a fight he works himself into a bloodlust and hurls a torch.
An Ember Worg is a beast of the Burning Steppes whose bite carries infection.
Venomtip Scorpids are beasts found in the Searing Gorge area. Their combat behavior includes Poison, a threat conveyed by the venom in their name and attack.
A Slavering Ember Worg is a beast of the Burning Steppes that tears at tendons.
Deathlash Scorpids are scorpid beasts of the Burning Steppes that sting with venom.
Giant Ember Worgs are beasts found in the Searing Gorge area. Their combat attack is Rend, setting them apart from Ember Worgs that use Infected Bite.
Firetail Scorpids are scorpid beasts of the Burning Steppes that sting with venom, as Deathlash Scorpids do.
Lava Crabs are small critters recorded across several regions, including the Searing Gorge and Burning Steppes. Their broad distribution sets them apart from the area's more localized beasts.
Flamekin Spitter spits venom at its foes.
Flamekin Sprite thrashes at its foes.
Flamekin Torcher hurls fireballs at its foes.
Flamekin Rager can go into a frenzy as its health falls.

Mathredis Firestar searches for ten librams written by Master Kariel Winthalus, scattered after the Scourge was unleashed upon Quel'Thalas. He offers to absorb a found libram's magic and craft an amalgamation of power, while warning that his price is high and he keeps most gathered components. He describes the vast energies as making his head throb, then tells the visitor to take what they desire and leave.
Deathmaw is a formidable beast with a tendon-ripping attack.
Terrorspark is a demon that attacks with fire magic and can summon Flamekin Torchers and Ragers into battle.
Volchan is a giant whose combat behavior includes Flamecrack; it also casts a fire shield while out of combat.

Kibler is an animal lover and salesman who tracks down exotic creatures for wealthy clients and domesticates them as pets. He keeps cages for his work and seeks help sourcing worg pups and spire spider eggs; he says he sent Bijou to gather eggs and has not heard from her in weeks.

Opus is a squawking beast who trades rumors about Kibler and Bijou: he urges listeners to ask Kibler about treasure, says Bijou knows where it is hidden, and laments that people sent to the Spire never return, like Bijou. His cough punctuates a squawk about needing to quit smoking, and he says Kibler is being investigated by G.E.T.A.

Tinkee Steamboil studies the dragonkin of the Burning Steppes and develops devices to investigate them, from capturing broodling essence to freezing and collecting dragon eggs. She is eager to test her inventions and proud when they work. Her research has an unnamed patron, whose displeasure she warns people not to risk.
Vahgruk is a Wind Rider Master in the Burning Steppes. He offers fast travel and quest-giver service; when attacked, he calls for guards and summons an enraged wyvern.

Mor'zul Bloodbringer is studying near the Altar of Storms and guides the work of binding a dreadsteed from Xoroth. He offers to scribe the required glyphs, asking for owlbeast blood to make the ink; his servant Gorzeeki prepares it. Mor'zul also directs materials to Gorzeeki for a summoning wheel, and remarks that the blood's taste is euphoric to him.

Gorzeeki Wildeyes is an eccentric associate in the dreadsteed-summoning work around Mor'zul. He speaks eagerly of Mor'zul's blood and the prospect of another parchment, and says he prefers keeping rodent blood warm in a living animal. He also treats an imp jar as a cherished keepsake, thanking its return and refusing to sell it. His shop offers shadowy potions for the journey to Lord Banehollow.

Franklin the Friendly presents a gentle, nature-minded face despite the lava around him, urging a visitor to enjoy the surroundings. A challenger addresses him as Klinfran the Crazed and dares him to reveal his true form, suggesting a fearsome identity beneath the friendly manner; the exchange does not establish what follows.

Elder Rumblerock speaks of the new year and bright moon as the time when the ancients awake. His seasonal greeting invites questions about where to find fellow elders Dawnstrider, Hammershout, Stormbrow and Winterhoof, while his farewell wishes the visitor well and offers a token. His words place him in an annual observance.

Elder Dawnstrider speaks of a past when his people hunted for glory and honor, and wonders whether that has truly changed. His exchange with visitors also includes homage and a token offered in return.

A seasonal flame warden serving the Alliance in the Burning Steppes. The warden invites visitors to honor the local festival flame and urges them to dishonor Horde fires, reflecting the Alliance side of the midsummer rivalry.

A seasonal flame keeper serving the Horde in the Burning Steppes. The keeper invites visitors to honor the local festival flame and urges them to dishonor Alliance fires, reflecting the Horde side of the midsummer rivalry.

place_records.text: You are in the Burning Steppes, a contested land in the Eastern Kingdoms where both the Alliance and the Horde hold settlements. Flame Crest is held by the Horde and Morgan's Vigil by the Alliance. Dragonkin, flamekin, scorpids, ogres and Blackrock soldiers are the main dangers.

You are in Dreadmaul Rock, a rocky part of the Burning Steppes. Firegut ogres, ogre mages and obsidian elementals roam it, and a malfunctioning mechanical reaver still lumbers among the stones. Oralius of Morgan's Vigil calls the Firegut ogres allies of the Blackrock orcs.

You are in the Ruins of Thaurissan, a ruined city in the Burning Steppes. Thaurissan agents, spies and firewalkers haunt it, along with War Reavers and Thauris Balgarr. A tormented voice in the ruins warns intruders away and speaks of the city's destruction.

You are in Flame Crest, a Horde settlement in the Burning Steppes, with a flight master, a spirit healer and a vendor. Tinkee Steamboil studies the dragonkin here and builds devices to capture broodling essence and freeze dragon eggs. Flamekin torchers and ragers are the troubles nearby.

You are in Blackrock Stronghold, a fortified Blackrock orc base in the Burning Steppes. Blackrock warlocks, slayers and battlemasters guard it, and Gruklash is among its most dangerous. A Blackrock informant named Grark Lorkrub is accused of betraying the Thorium Brotherhood.
You are in the Pillar of Ash, a stretch of the Burning Steppes where Blackrock sorcerers, soldiers, warlocks and worgs roam. Greater obsidian elementals are among the troubles here.

You are in Blackrock Mountain, a fiery mountain in the Burning Steppes full of old Dark Iron works. The ghostly architect Franclorn Forgewright claims the stonewrought design of those works, and Bodley, a ghost and former mercenary, wants to set things right. Lothos Riftwaker studies the rifts around the mountain. Flamescale wyrmkin and Blackrock drakes are the dangers, and a spirit healer is here.

You are in the Altar of Storms, a place of summoning rites in the Burning Steppes. Mor'zul Bloodbringer studies here, working to bind a dreadsteed from Xoroth, and his servant Gorzeeki Wildeyes prepares the ink. Blackrock warlocks and Gruklash are the dangers.

You are in Morgan's Vigil, an Alliance settlement in the Burning Steppes, with a gryphon master, a weaponsmith and repairs. Marshal Maxwell and Oralius direct the Alliance campaign against Blackrock Spire and the Firegut ogres. Jalinda Sprig is trying to get an expedition into Blackrock Depths, though Overmaster Pyron has badly hurt the mages she sent.

You are in Slither Rock, a place in the Burning Steppes where Cyrus Therepentous, a fire-loving dragonkin, craves the molten heat of Blackrock's depths. He demands proof of worth from anyone seeking the Black Dragonflight and speaks with cutting contempt. Black broodlings are the danger here.

You are in Terror Wing Path, a route in the Burning Steppes where black dragonspawn, black wyrmkin and black broodlings roam. Venomtip scorpids, ember worgs and Firegut ogres are here too. A malfunctioning mechanical reaver is also here.

You are in Draco'dar, a place of lava in the Burning Steppes. Franklin the Friendly keeps a gentle, nature-minded face here, though challengers call him Klinfran the Crazed. Flamescale broodlings, searscale drakes and firetail scorpids are the dangers, and Hematos roams here too.
